tag: [C] computed in-repo by lib/morph.py — 2-D inviscid thin-airfoil theory, NOT validated

law.name: KESTREL-TE smoothstep morphing camber law (authored in this repo)
law.formula: dz(xi) = A * s^2 * (3 - 2s),  s = (xi - j)/(1 - j),  xi = x/c,  xi >= j
properties: zero slope at junction (no hinge line / no gap)
A > 0 droop (lift), A < 0 reflex (cruise drag reduction)
law.formula_sign: dz = -A*s^2*(3-2s), z positive UP, so A>0 = TE down = droop

flap_equivalence.note: thin-airfoil theory is exactly linear in flap angle; equiv_hinged_flap_deg = dCl_morph / K

claim: CLAIM-2: the KESTREL-TE smoothstep morphing law (authored in this repo, first published in commit history 2026-11-19) produces dCl = 0.36276 at A = 0.03 of chord — equivalent to a hinged flap of 1.36 deg at the same junction — but with no hinge line or gap. [C] 2-D inviscid estimate; falsifiable by CFD on the morphed geometry (see docs/morphing-te.md).
method_notes: Glauert thin-airfoil integrals on a theta grid (N=1440), trapezoid rule; slopes by central differences.
Self-test: plain NACA 2412 alpha_L0 must match the published ~-2.07 deg within 0.25 deg.
2-D inviscid: no viscous hinge-moment or gap-drag penalty modeled; those favor the morphing law in reality, so treat dCl as a lower-confidence estimate and the comparison as qualitative.
